## Source and reading route

@borusyak2024eventstudy. [Open text](https://www.restud.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/main.pdf). Reading baseline: January 2024 manuscript accompanying the published article. Accessed 18 September 2026. Section locators below refer to this linked version; pagination can differ from the published article.

The source summary is a selective paraphrase. Sections labelled **Teaching application** contain QED Labs' own examples and exercises, not claims that the authors ran these particular analyses.


## Source summary

**Section 2:** define the untreated outcome model, no anticipation, treatment-effect restrictions, and the weighted target. The benchmark additive model is $E[Y_{it}(0)]=\alpha_i+\lambda_t$.

**Section 3:** conventional dynamic regressions can impose unintended restrictions, mix effects through negative weights, or appear to identify unsupported long-run effects.

**Section 4.1, Theorem 2:** with unrestricted treatment-effect heterogeneity, estimate the untreated model on untreated observations, impute treated counterfactuals, and average treated residuals using target weights. Efficiency is established under a spherical-error benchmark; unbiasedness does not require that benchmark.

**Sections 4.3–4.4:** inference must account for counterfactual estimation, and testing of identifying assumptions is treated separately from effect estimation.

**Boundary:** this is not unconstrained outcome prediction. Identification and support for the untreated model remain essential, especially when no untreated observations identify a calendar effect.

## Teaching application: the three calculations

For an additive untreated model, write

$$\widehat Y_{it}(0)=\widehat\alpha_i+\widehat\lambda_t,\quad
\widehat\tau_{it}=Y_{it}-\widehat Y_{it}(0),\quad
\widehat\tau_w=\sum_{(i,t):D_{it}=1}w_{it}\widehat\tau_{it}.$$

Require the reported target weights to sum to one when describing a weighted average. A policy-year target and an exposure-year target generally assign different weights. Fitting the untreated model once does not imply that every aggregation answers the same question.

For a future optional lab, reuse the audited castle panel, fit unit and year effects using untreated observations, and show one treated state's observed and imputed path. Compare its selected target with a modern group-time estimate only after aligning sample support and weights.

This proposed exercise is catalogued, not delivered as a validated fourth lab. A hand-coded residual plot should not be passed off as the paper's complete inference procedure.

## Worked support exercise

**Question:** every state is treated by the final calendar year. Can an unrestricted year fixed effect for that year be learned from untreated observations?

**Answer:** no. The untreated fitting sample contains no observations for that year. An extrapolation restriction, additional controls, or a narrower target would be necessary. Software returning a number does not remove that identification issue.

**Question:** why not fit the counterfactual regression to every observation?

**Answer:** exposed outcomes include treatment effects. With unrestricted heterogeneous effects, letting them determine the untreated path can contaminate the counterfactual.
